lesson.subject: numeracy
lesson.title: Plotting Points to Draw Shapes
lesson.subtitle: Term 4 Week 2, Session 2
lesson.fileName: Session 2 - Plotting Points to Draw Shapes.pptx

plan.curriculum: Mathematics 2.0, Space, Year 5 (VC2M5SP02) and Year 6 (VC2M6SP02): plotting points from coordinates and listing coordinates in order to complete a polygon
plan.shape: example-first, then a practice round of missing corners, because joining in order and reasoning about a missing vertex are both new
plan.criticalFeature: join the points in the order they are listed, then back to the start
decisionPoints: the choice check: which list draws a square?
the hinge: the fourth corner of a rectangle
plan.anchor: across the corridor, then up the stairs: (x, y), and the numbers sit on the lines
plan.catchUp: Missed Session 1? Show the anchor on the big grid and plot one point together (across, then up) before the I Do.

studentTools: A ruler and a sharp pencil for every student
Printed Worksheet for every student; Extension and Supported Worksheet as needed
routineIcons: Write it, chin it, show me
boardSetup: The anchor on the board: across the corridor, then up the stairs, (x, y)
A large grid drawn or projected for plotting together

resources.label: Worksheet
resources.description: Your turn. Plot and join shapes, read a shape's corners, find missing corners, fix a mistake and design a garden bed.
resources.title: Plotting Points to Draw Shapes
resources.subtitle: Plot each point, then join them in order.

example.prompt: Plot and join (1, 1), (4, 1), (1, 3). Name the shape.
steps: Plot each point: across, then up.
Join them in order, then back to the start.
Three straight sides: a triangle.

items.prompt: Plot and join in order: (1, 1), (6, 1), (6, 4), (1, 4). Name the shape.
Plot and join in order: (2, 0), (6, 0), (4, 5). Name the shape.
Write the coordinates of each corner of the house.

example.prompt: A rectangle has corners at (1, 1), (5, 1) and (5, 3). Find the fourth corner.
steps: It is straight above (1, 1): across 1.
It is level with (5, 3): up 3.
So it is (1, 3).

items.prompt: A rectangle has corners at (2, 1), (7, 1) and (7, 6). Where is the fourth corner? Sketch it if it helps.
Leo found the fourth corner of the rectangle (3, 2), (8, 2), (8, 5). Find his mistake and fix it.
items.answer: He swapped the two numbers. Across comes first: it is (3, 5), above (3, 2) and level with (8, 5).

example.prompt: A sandpit is a square with sides 3 long. One corner is at (2, 2). Where is the corner to its right?
steps: Going right changes the across number.
The corner is (5, 2).

items.prompt: A garden bed is a rectangle 4 long and 2 wide. Its bottom-left corner is at (1, 1). Find its other corners.
Which point makes a right-angled triangle with (1, 1) and (5, 1)?
items.explain: (5, 4) is straight above (5, 1), so the corner at (5, 1) is a right angle.

resources.label: Extension
resources.description: Early finisher option. Side lengths and perimeter from coordinates, halfway points and your own symmetrical shape, with worked examples.
resources.title: Extension: Shapes on the Grid
resources.subtitle: Use the coordinates to measure.

example.prompt: How long is the side from (2, 3) to (7, 3)?
steps: The up number stays 3, so the side goes across.
Across from 2 to 7.
7 - 2 = 5 units.

items.prompt: A rectangle has corners (1, 1), (7, 1), (7, 4) and (1, 4). Find its length, width and perimeter.
A square has corners (2, 2), (7, 2), (7, 7) and (2, 7). What is its perimeter? What is its area?

example.prompt: What point is halfway between (2, 4) and (8, 4)?
steps: The up number stays 4.
Halfway between 2 and 8 is 5.

items.prompt: What point is halfway between (1, 6) and (9, 6)?
What point is halfway between (4, 1) and (4, 7)?
Which point is the centre of the square (0, 0), (6, 0), (6, 6), (0, 6)?
items.explain: Halfway across is 3 and halfway up is 3.

steps: Draw a line of symmetry down the grid.
Plot corners on one side, then mirror them.
List all the corners in order.

items.prompt: Design a symmetrical shape with 6 corners. List its corners in order so a partner can draw it.
items.answer: Check the list is in order, across first, and the shape is symmetrical.

resources.label: Supported Worksheet
resources.description: For students who need more guidance: fewer points, the first point plotted, and a hint on every question.
resources.title: Drawing Shapes: Step by Step
resources.subtitle: Plot one point at a time.

steps: Plot (1, 1): across 1, up 1.
Plot the next two the same way.
Join them with a ruler, then back to the start.

items.hint: The first point is done for you.
Across first, then up, for every point.

example.prompt: Find the fourth corner of the square.
steps: The missing corner is above (1, 1), so across 1.
It is level with (4, 4), so up 4.

items.prompt: Find the fourth corner of the rectangle.
items.hint: It is above A, so its across number is 1.

items.prompt: Find the fourth corner of the square.
items.hint: It is above A and level with C.

slides.notes: Session 2 of our coordinates week: today we plot points and join them to draw shapes.
Before you start, put boards, markers, a ruler and a pencil on every desk. Print the Worksheet for everyone, and a few copies of the Extension and the Supported Worksheet.

beats: SAY: Let's warm up with last week's angles again.
ASK: How big is the reflex angle marked with a question mark?
20 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 290
SCAN boards, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal and move straight on.
Less -> trace all the way round: 360 take away the inside angle. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: It's 290 degrees, because 360 take away 70 is 290.
Tick it or fix it.
trap: writing 110, from 180.
Fix: trace the full turn, and they redo it from 360.
notes.prep: Review of Week 1 angles (the request named the focus). Keep the review under 6 minutes.

beats: ASK: How big is angle a?
20 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 125
SCAN boards, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal and move straight on.
Less -> point to the straight line that a and 55 share,
then subtract from 180. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: It's 125 degrees. Angle a sits next to 55 on a straight line,
and 180 take away 55 is 125. Tick it or fix it.
trap: writing 55, the opposite angle.
Fix: ask whether a is opposite or next to 55, and they redo it.
notes.prep: Week 1 review: angles where two lines cross.

beats: ASK: What is the name of each angle: 95, 35 and 185 degrees?
20 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: obtuse, acute, reflex
SCAN boards, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal, then on to Fluency.
Less -> hold up the name chart and compare each with 90 and 180. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: 95 is obtuse, 35 is acute, and 185 is reflex,
because it's past a straight line. Tick it or fix it.
trap: calling 185 obtuse.
Fix: ask whether it is past a straight line, and they rename it reflex.

beats: SAY: Now for our four times table.
Write each answer as fast as you can.
ASK: What is 4 times 8?
8 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 32
SCAN boards.
80%+ -> reveal, then the next one.
Less -> double 8, then double again. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: It's 32. Tick it or fix it.
trap: writing 28 or 36.
Fix: double 8 to get 16, double again to get 32, and they rewrite it.
notes.prep: Times tables fluency. Keep the whole block under 5 minutes.

beats: SAY: Here's the next one.
ASK: What is 6 times 4?
8 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 24
SCAN boards.
80%+ -> reveal, then the next one.
Less -> double 6, then double again. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: It's 24. Tick it or fix it.
trap: writing 20.
Fix: count on one more 4 from 5 times 4, and they rewrite it.
notes.prep: Brisk: one line of feedback, then the next.

beats: SAY: Now a division. Think: how many fours make 48?
ASK: What is 48 divided by 4?
8 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 12
SCAN boards.
80%+ -> reveal, then the learning intention.
Less -> halve 48, then halve again. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: It's 12. Tick it or fix it.
trap: writing 11.
Fix: check: 12 times 4 is 48, and they rewrite it.
notes.prep: Brisk: one line of feedback, then the next.

slides.learningIntention: We are learning to plot points from coordinates and join them to draw shapes.
successCriteria: I can plot a list of points on a grid.
I can draw a shape by joining points in the order they are listed.
I can find a missing corner and explain how I know.

beats: POINT to the learning intention.
SAY: Yesterday we read and plotted single points.
Today we join points to make shapes.
SAY: Let's read our I can statements together.
Cue: Everyone, together, on three.
SAY: The first one is where we start,
and the second one is our big goal today.
notes.prep: SC1 plotting is reachable for everyone; SC2 joining in order is the core and the exit evidence; SC3 reasoning about a missing corner is the stretch.

slides.title: Join the dots
slides.prompt: Join A, B, C, D in order. What shape do you get?

beats: POINT to each point in turn.
SAY: Here are four points, A, B, C and D.
Picture joining them in order with a ruler.
ASK: What shape do you get if you join A,
B, C, D in order, and back to A?
15 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: a square
SCAN boards for square.
80%+ -> draw it on the board and move on.
Less -> trace A to B to C to D in the air together. Re-ask.
SAY: It's a square. Now, what would happen if I joined A to C first?
The order changes the drawing, and that's our big idea today.
trap: saying rectangle.
Fix: count the squares along each side, 4 and 4, and they rename it.
notes.prep: The launch comes after the LI: order matters when joining points. Under 4 minutes.

slides.meaning: A corner of a shape, where two sides meet. More than one are called vertices.

notes.answer: a corner, where two sides meet
beats: POINT to the word.
SAY: This word is vertex. Say it with me: vertex.
SAY: A vertex is a corner of a shape, where two sides meet.
When there's more than one, we call them vertices.
ASK: How many vertices does this triangle have?
5 sec. Cue: Fingers at your chest... show me.
EXPECT: 3
trap: counting the sides and the corners together.
Fix: touch only the corners, and they count again.
notes.prep: Mathematicians plot the vertices, then join them. Vertex and corner both work in speech today.

slides.title: Plot and join
steps: Plot each point: across, then up.
Join them in the order listed.
Join the last point back to the first.
Name the shape.

beats: MODEL plotting A (2, 1), B (7, 1), C (2, 5).
SAY: Let me plot these three points.
For each one, I go across first, then up.
MODEL joining A to B to C, then back to A.
SAY: Now I join them in the order they're listed,
and I always finish by joining the last point back to the first.
ASK: What shape have I drawn?
10 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: a triangle. ACCEPT: right-angled triangle
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: It's a right-angled triangle.
The corner at A is square: one side goes across, one goes straight up.
trap: leaving the shape open.
Fix: ask where the last point joins to, and they close it.
notes.stretch: Move one point to make an isosceles triangle.
notes.help: Tick each point as you plot it.
notes.prep: Plot, then join in order, then close the shape. SC1 and SC2.

slides.title: Find the missing corner
steps: Plot the three corners you know.
D is straight above A, so its across number is A's: 1.
D is level with C, so its up number is C's: 5.
Write D as (1, 5).

beats: POINT to A, B and C.
SAY: This rectangle has lost a corner. We know A, B and C.
MODEL tracing up from A, and across from C.
SAY: The missing corner D sits straight above A,
so it goes across 1, just like A.
And it's level with C, so it goes up 5, just like C.
ASK: So what are the coordinates of D?
10 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: (1, 5)
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: It's 1, 5. We borrowed the across number from A,
and the up number from C.
trap: writing (5, 1).
Fix: trace up from A and across from C, and they rewrite it.
notes.stretch: If the rectangle were a square, what would D be?
notes.help: Lay one ruler up from A and one across from C.
notes.prep: Reasoning about a missing vertex: borrow one number from each neighbour. SC3.

slides.title: Which list draws a square?
slides.prompt: Join the points in order. Point to A, B or C

options.misconception: ignores the order: the right points, but joined they make crossed lines
checks for square corners but not equal sides: this is a rectangle

beats: SAY: Each list has four points.
Picture joining them in order. Which one makes a square?
ASK: Which list draws a square when you join the points in order?
20 sec. Cue: Voices off. Point... now. Hold your point.
EXPECT: pointing to A
SCAN the room, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal, then cold call one student: Why isn't it B?
Less -> sketch B on the big grid
in order so they see the crossed lines. Re-ask.
REVEAL after pointing is scanned.
SAY: It's A. B has the same points, but in the wrong order,
so its lines cross over.
C is a rectangle, because its sides are 3 and 2.
trap: pointing to B.
Fix: draw B in order together, and they choose again.
notes.prep: First decision point: B means order is ignored; C means equal sides are not checked.

slides.title: Find the missing corner
slides.ask: What are the coordinates of the missing corner D?
slides.pivot: trace up from one corner and across from another with two rulers
slides.followUp: cold call one board: Which corner gave you the across number?

items.say: It's 0, 5. It sits right on the line going up.
It's 2, 3. In a parallelogram, the top side matches the bottom side.

say: Write the missing corner on your board each time.
trap: swapping the two numbers.
Fix: ask which number is across, and they rewrite it.
notes.stretch: Find the perimeter of each shape in units.
notes.help: Lay one ruler up from a corner and one across from another.
notes.prep: Guided practice from typical to edge: a corner on the axis, then a parallelogram. SC2 and SC3.

notes.answer: (7, 3). (3, 7) means across and up were swapped
beats: SAY: This one is just for you.
It's a rectangle, and D is missing.
ASK: What are the coordinates of D?
20 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: (7, 3)
SCAN every board, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal, then Your turn.
Less -> trace down from C and across from A together. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: It's 7, 3. D is below C, so across 7,
and level with A, so up 3. Tick it or fix it.
trap: writing (3, 7).
Fix: ask which number is across, and they rewrite it.
notes.prep: The hinge before independent work. Anyone who wrote (3, 7) starts on the Supported Worksheet with the teacher.

slides.title: Your turn
slides.task: Plot, join and find the corners on your worksheet.

beats: POINT to the steps.
SAY: Read each question carefully, solve it carefully, then check your answers.
SAY: If you finish, the Extension is your early finisher option.
Let's read the steps together. Cue: Everyone, together, on three.
CIRCULATE and ask: Which order did you join the points in?
TIME: 20 minutes. Stop everyone once at 10 minutes to share a strategy.
trap: joining points out of order.
Fix: tick each point in the list as they join it, and they redraw it.
notes.stretch: Extension: side lengths and perimeter from coordinates, halfway points and your own symmetrical shape.
notes.help: Supported Worksheet: fewer points, the first point plotted, and a hint on every question.
notes.prep: Independent practice: plot and join, missing corners, a mistake and a design problem. The sheet is evidence for SC2 and SC3.

slides.title: Show what you know
questions: A square has corners (1, 2), (4, 2) and (4, 5). Find the fourth.

beats: SAY: Here's the last one. Work it out on your own board.
ASK: What is the fourth corner of this square?
25 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: (1, 5)
RECORD who writes (5, 1) or leaves it blank.
They start tomorrow's check with the teacher.
trap: writing (5, 1).
Fix: none now. Record the name for tomorrow.
notes.prep: Exit evidence for SC2 and SC3: a new square with no picture drawn.

slides.reflectionPrompt: Tell your partner why the order of the points matters.

notes.answer: open - listen for joining in a different order makes a different drawing
beats: SAY: Let's read our I can statements together.
Cue: Everyone, together, on three.
ASK: How sure are you that you can
draw a shape from a list of points?
5 sec. Cue: Thumbs only, voices off. Show me... now.
EXPECT: thumbs up, sideways or down
RECORD each thumb down beside the exit board.
A thumb up with (5, 1) on the board matters most.
ASK: Why does the order of the points matter?
20 sec. Cue: Partner B first. You have 20 seconds. Go.
EXPECT: joining in a different order makes a different drawing
notes.prep: Read the self-assessment beside the exit evidence. Tomorrow's first check comes from both.
